artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan (~7h) for the out-of-repository pathspec containment fix, its exit-code contract extension, the one live caller's exit-code branch, and an enforcement lint.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a repository-containment predicate to a git pathspec filter, resolve the pathspec's PARENT directory with realpath and leave the final component unresolved. Verified empirically: an in-repo leaf symlink whose target is outside the repo is a LEGAL `git add` argument (rc=0, staged as a symlink), so a leaf-resolving `realpath -m --relative-to=$ROOT -- $p` predicate classifies it as out-of-repo and drops it -- a false-positive regression. A path THROUGH an in-repo symlinked directory is fatal to git (`fatal: pathspec ... is beyond a symbolic link`) and SHOULD be dropped. The parent-resolving form (`realpath -m --relative-to=$ROOT_RESOLVED -- $(dirname -- $p)`, out-of-repo when the result is empty, `..`, or `../*`) agrees with git add's own accept/reject verdict on all 13 pathspec shapes tested, including `..`-laundered paths and a sibling directory sharing the root as a literal prefix (`<root>-backup`), which a naive string-prefix comparison gets wrong. Resolve the root through the same realpath call, never raw.
